candidates.claim: Authentication-state changes can race after this cancellation check and still cache a stale token.
candidates.repro: Minimal repro: use a custom `AuthenticationStateProvider` that completes `RequestAccessToken`, pauses the handler immediately after this check, raises `NotifyAuthenticationStateChanged` on another thread, then resumes the handler.

candidates.head: 2edf3761692afe15475075eb2fc0088566162045
candidates.claim: P2 — The new early header snapshot can attach an obsolete token after a concurrent refresh completes.
candidates.effect: request 1 sends expired/obsolete bearer token A even though the shared handler has already refreshed to B. Frozen merge-base/base-tip read `_cachedHeader` at attachment time and send B under the same completed-refresh ordering.
candidates.repro: prime the handler with nearly-expired token A; start request 1 and pause it immediately after line 65; allow request 2 to refresh and fully commit token/header B; resume request 1. Request 1 observes valid `_lastToken` B and skips refresh, but line 92 attaches its earlier local snapshot A.

candidates.head: 2edf3761692afe15475075eb2fc0088566162045
candidates.claim: Concurrent requests can use different invalidation tokens, allowing a stale result to remain cacheable.
candidates.effect:
Only the CTS still stored in `_authenticationStateChangedCts` is canceled. The other request sees an uncanceled token at line 77 and writes its stale token into `_lastToken` and `_cachedHeader`, defeating the fix.
Fix: synchronize CTS acquisition, authentication-state invalidation, and the cancellation-check/cache commit using the same lock, or use an equivalent atomic generation mechanism that makes the check and commit indivisible relative to invalidation.
candidates.repro: Issue two concurrent authorized requests while the cache is empty. If both evaluate the unsynchronized `??=` before either assignment is visible, each can retain a different CTS token. Raise `AuthenticationStateChanged`, then complete the request whose CTS was overwritten with an old token.
